subject: Request: limited SLO carve-out for moderation/tool-call failures
messages:
From: Lexi Park <lexi@acme-ai.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, rachel.kim@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 25 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: limited SLO carve-out for moderation/tool-call failures

Hi Jonas / Rachel,

Thanks again for yesterday's sync. We're kicking a pilot of an agent feature that invokes an external content moderation tool and uses Redwood's tool-calling to enrich responses. During initial tests we've observed a ~0.6% increase in end-to-end latency and a small number of failed enrichments when the moderation tool times out (~150ms extra on retries).

Because the feature is customer-facing, our legal and security teams want a temporary, narrowly-scoped SLO carve-out that:
- excludes moderation-tool-induced structured-output failures from latency SLO penalties for 30 days
- allows up to 1% of requests to be retried/filtered without counting as downtime for the integration's downstream calls

I've attached a small impact CSV showing request distribution and a short appendix describing the retry behaviour. Can Redwood review and tell us what form the carve-out would need to take (contractual addendum vs. operational exception)? Also: what observability hooks do you need from our side?

Lexi
Lexi Park
Director, Product
Acme AI
Attachments: acme_inc_slo-impact.csv (csv)
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Lexi Park <lexi@acme-ai.com>
Cc: rachel.kim@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 25 Jan 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: limited SLO carve-out for moderation/tool-call failures

Lexi — thanks for the appendix and the timing breakdown, that helps. Short answers up front: we can offer a limited carve-out but it must be timeboxed, scoped to the tool-calling path you described, and conditioned on instrumentation and retry limits.

Couple of clarifying items we need from you before we scope language:
- exact endpoint(s) your integration uses (URL patterns)
- expected qps during the pilot and peak window (we need to model burst impact)
- whether the moderation call happens synchronously on the critical path or can be async with graceful degradation

Operational controls we propose if you want a carve-out:
1) Redwood will exclude errors attributable to an upstream moderation tool from the application-level latency SLO only if your integration includes a request-level trace id on X-Trace header and Redwood receives the 4xx/5xx downstream tag in the trace.
2) Timeboxed: 30 days max; can request one 14-day extension with signoff from Redwood ops and customer security.
3) Retry policy: max 2 retries, exponential backoff; each retry must be tagged.
4) Fallback: structured output must include an explicit "moderation_unavailable" field so we can differentiate content-moderation-induced structured-output failures from model failures.

I'll loop in Laura and our ops lead to get legal language and an Ops ticket. In the meantime, can you drop the endpoint list and peak QPS?

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
From: rachel.kim@redwood.com <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 02 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Request: limited SLO carve-out for moderation/tool-call failures

Laura / Sean — forwarding Lexi's request and Jonas' proposed operational controls. I drafted a short carve-out clause and attached it as a docx to review (proposed_slo_carveout_draft.docx). Key points: 30-day window, 1% cap on affected requests, instrumentation requirements (X-Trace header + downstream tag), retries limited to 2, and a required fallback field in structured output.

Operational concerns from Sean: we need a detection rule so that we only exclude incidents where the failure is clearly from the upstream moderation tool. Sean, can you confirm what logs or error codes we need to rely on? If we can't reliably attribute, we shouldn't exclude the incident.

Also proposing: Redwood will require Acme to sign an Ops addendum and accept a small monthly uplift (one-off) to cover extra support during the pilot. Suggested billing note will be handled by Finance if Laura signs off.

Rachel Kim
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: limited SLO carve-out for moderation/tool-call failures

Lexi — thanks for the additional info and for being responsive on the instrumentation notes. After reviewing with Ops and Legal we can approve a 30-day limited carve-out with the following mandatory conditions:

1) Attribution: Acme must include a trace id (X-Trace) and Redwood will only apply the carve-out when the trace contains a downstream 4xx/5xx tag that matches one of the provided endpoint URL patterns.
2) Retry limits: maximum of 2 retries per request. Any additional retries will not be eligible for exclusion.
3) Fallback: responses must include an explicit "moderation_unavailable": true boolean in structured outputs when the moderation enrichment is skipped.
4) Timebox: effective for 30 days from the signed addendum. One 14-day extension may be requested 5 days before expiry with Ops signoff.
5) Billing: Acme accepts a one-time pilot support fee (amount in addendum).

Please review the attached DocuSign link and return a signed copy. We'll open JIRA OPS-1289 to track the instrumentation and detection rule work on our side. If anything is unclear, happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
